why: The student reads `if (x > 0);` as if the semicolon only ends the clause, so they treat the println as the if's body. In Java the lone `;` is the whole body, so the println always runs, and the code prints positive, negative and checked.

concepts.quote: positive is not printed, because x > 0 is false.
concepts.why: The answer misses that the `;` after `if (x > 0)` is an empty statement that forms the whole then branch, so the println is not controlled by the if.

concepts.quote: positive is not printed, because x > 0 is false
concepts.why: The answer treats the next line as the if body even though Java ends the body at the semicolon, so the predicted output is wrong.
The answer evaluates -3 > 0 as false, which is correct.
The answer says nothing about assignment.
